dns.identicalEgressAddressesMergedTheirC: Identical egress addresses are merged. Their count depends on actual resolution paths and does not equal the number of DNS servers configured on your device.
link.medianBrowserHttpRequestTimeAcrossS: Median browser HTTP request time across successful requests in 8 rounds, not ICMP Ping. Cross-origin restrictions or timeouts may produce unknown results.
ping.verifyBeforeMeasurement: Complete human verification to start this measurement.
ping.someNodesHaveFinishedViewReturnedRe: Some nodes have not finished. View returned results or test again.
ping.enterAnIpAddressOrDomain: Enter an IP address or domain
ping.searchCountryCityOneOnlineProbeSele: Search by country or city. One online probe is selected per city, up to 50 custom cities.
ping.optimizedModePrioritizes2MainlandCh: Optimized mode prioritizes 2 mainland China cities for comparison. Other regions favor major cloud providers, falling back to online nodes. Global mode adds up to 2 per continent; single-continent mode adds up to 5. Identical combinations reuse results for 60 seconds. A failed ping alone does not prove censorship.
ping.mainlandChinaCitiesAreCurrentlyOnli: mainland China cities are currently online.
ping.nodesReturnedAverageLatencyHighestF: nodes returned · Average latency, highest first; missing values last
webrtc.browserDoesSupportWebrtcSoCheckCa: This browser does not support WebRTC, so the check cannot run.
webrtc.publicCandidateAddressCollectedBr: No public candidate address collected. Browser restrictions, UDP blocking or disabled WebRTC may be responsible; this does not establish safety.
webrtc.udpEgressCollectedButHttpBaseline: UDP egress collected, but the HTTP baseline failed. Cannot determine whether they match.
webrtc.udpAddressDiffersHttpEgressCheckP: A UDP address differs from HTTP egress. Check your proxy routing rules; different egress does not necessarily mean a leak.
webrtc.theSampledPublicUdpEgressMatchesH: The sampled public UDP egress matches HTTP egress.
webrtc.webrtcUsesIceStunDiscoverAddresse: WebRTC uses ICE/STUN to discover addresses for peer-to-peer connections. STUN usually uses UDP. If a proxy handles only TCP, candidates may expose another public egress. This page creates only a data channel and does not request camera or microphone permission.
webrtc.udpConnectionlessTransportProtoco: UDP is a connectionless transport protocol. A STUN server returns the public mapped address it observes to the client. This tool uses Google and Cloudflare STUN, collects ICE candidates and compares them with HTTP egress. Local addresses hidden by mDNS are not reported as public IPs.
webrtc.howITellIfThereLeak: How can I tell if there is a leak?
webrtc.differentEgressIndicatesDifferent: Different egress only indicates different UDP and HTTP routes, which may be intentional. Check ISP, region and proxy rules. No public address may mean UDP is blocked or the browser restricted collection; this does not establish safety.
webrtc.howDoIFixALeak: How do I fix a leak?
webrtc.checkUdpForwardingTunTrafficHandl: Check UDP forwarding, TUN traffic handling and IPv6 rules in your client. Firefox can disable media.peerconnection.enabled in about:config; Brave can disable non-proxied UDP. Disabling WebRTC affects video conferencing and similar features, so correcting proxy routing is preferable.
webrtc.whyDoProxyTunModesGiveDifferentRe: Why do proxy and TUN modes give different results?
webrtc.systemProxyVirtualNetworkAdapterM: System proxy and virtual network adapter modes handle different traffic scopes. STUN may be unable to send traffic in some proxy modes, while TUN mode can expose the actual UDP route. Check DNS as well; a single WebRTC result is not a complete privacy audit.

speedtest.title: Speed test
speedtest.description: Measure download, upload, idle latency, and latency under load.
speedtest.openSpeedtestDescription: Free, officially hosted download, upload, and latency tests.
speedtest.panelFailed: The panel could not load. Try again or switch to Cloudflare.
speedtest.openSpeedtestNotice: After loading, use the panel's start button to test. OpenSpeedTest manages data usage. Stopping, switching services, or moving to the background closes the panel.
speedtest.curveLabel: {0} average speed over time, in Mbps
speedtest.trafficNotice: Up to {0} download and {1} upload per test, about {2} seconds each. Transfers finish early at the data limit. Starts only when clicked; stop at any time.
speedtest.methodNotice: Results measure browser-to-Cloudflare HTTP throughput and depend on your proxy, device, and route. Single and multiple requests may reuse HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connections. Leaving the page or switching to the background stops the test.
speedtest.uploadNotice: Upload speed and data update after successful requests; interrupted transfers may consume more. Data totals count payload only, excluding protocol overhead.
speedtest.invalidResponse: The test endpoint did not return valid measurement data
speedtest.noSamples: No valid speed samples were collected
speedtest.failed: Test incomplete. Check that your network or proxy can reach speed.cloudflare.com and try again.
airport.title: Airport audit
airport.description: Paste a subscription to audit a whole airport: entry mix, datacenter cost, measured routes and whether its claims hold
airport.privacyNote: The subscription is parsed in your browser. Passwords, UUIDs and other credentials are never uploaded; the server only receives entry addresses.
airport.inputPlaceholder: Paste base64 subscription, node URI list, Clash YAML or sing-box JSON, or a subscription link
airport.urlDetected: This is a subscription link. Browsers cannot read it directly (subscription servers block cross-site reads). The site server can fetch it once: the link is used for this single request and is not cached or logged. You can also export the content from your client and paste it.
airport.parseEmpty: No nodes recognized. Check that you pasted subscription content.
airport.archetypeDesc.line: Most nodes enter through domestic relays or premium lines, so the user-to-airport leg is optimized.
airport.archetypeDesc.partial_line: Some nodes use relay or premium-line entries; the rest connect directly overseas.
airport.archetypeDesc.direct: No domestic relays or premium-line entries. Every node is a direct overseas host or CDN proxy, so peak-hour speed depends on ordinary international links.
airport.archetypeDesc.unknown: Entry addresses could not be resolved or identified.
airport.kindsNote: The entry is the server your device connects to; it decides the route of your leg to the airport.
airport.mismatch.iplc: Named as private line/IPLC, but the entry is {0} ({1})
airport.mismatch.relay: Named as relay, but the entry is {0} ({1})
airport.mismatchNote: IPLC/IEPL entries sit inside China or on a carrier private network; relay entries are domestic or premium-line hosts. CDN proxies and direct overseas hosts do not qualify.
airport.routeNote: Measured from China Telecom, Unicom and Mobile probes to the airport entry — the path your traffic actually takes. One sample per entry datacenter.
airport.routeSkipped: Every entry is a CDN proxy; the route depends on the CDN edge assigned, so no single-point measurement is run.
airport.exitNote: Exit (landing) IP purity and unlocks are checked on the home page after connecting to a specific node.
overview.tsx.airportAudit: Paste a subscription to check an airport's entry routes, cost and claims
